entry.title: 0.email frontend is built using react-router framework.
entry.summary:
In this article, we will review how 0.email frontend is built using react-router framework. We will look at: react-router in package.json
What is react-router?
I found that 0.email uses react-router framework by looking at its scripts objects in package.json file. { "name": "@zero/mail", "version": "0.1.0", "private": true, "type": "module", "scripts": { "dev": "react-router dev", "build": "react-router build", "start": "wrangler dev --port 3000 --show-interactive-dev-session=false", "types": "wrangler types", "deploy": "wrangler deploy", "lint": "eslint ." },
As you can there is dev and build scripts in the above code snippets using react-router. React-router is a multi-strategy router for React bridging the gap from React 18 to React 19. You can use it maximally as a React framework or as minimally as you want. You can learn more about react-router React Router is a multi-strategy router for React. There are three primary ways, or “modes”, to use it in your app. Across the docs you’ll see these icons indicating which mode the content is relevant to: Framework
Data
Declarative
Learn more about picking a mode When you choose framework as your mode, you can create a project using the command below: npx create-react-router@latest my-react-router-app
Now change into the new directory and start the app cd my-react-router-app npm i npm run dev
You can now open your browser to http://localhost:5173 You can learn more about framework-mode Hey, my name is Ramu Narasinga. I study codebase architecture in large open-source projects. Email: ramu.narasinga@gmail.com Build Shadcn CLI from scratch.
